body:
## Thesis

The evidence fingerprint that binds local receipts to "the tree I verified" hashes the agent's own scratch directory. Any tool that writes into `.qwen/` (or an equivalent per-agent working dir) inside a consumer repository moves the fingerprint without a single repository file changing, so every fingerprint-bound receipt is stale before it can be used. In a session that keeps working, "all three receipts fresh on the final tree" is unreachable by construction.

## Measured A/B in a consumer tree (see `00-fingerprint-ab.txt`)

| Step | Fingerprint | Changed? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | `93aea5fb89be5710…` | — |
| create `.qwen/tmp/fp-probe.txt` (no repo file touched) | `28b1489a610326f7…` | **yes** |
| delete the probe file | `93aea5fb89be5710…` | restored |

(The absolute value depends on the tree state at run time; the pair above is quoted from the attached transcript, which also shows the full hashes.) The set of paths feeding the hash already contained one agent-scratch entry in a normal working session: `.qwen/tmp/s-<uuid>/qwen-skill-args-loop.txt`.

## Why it is designed this way and where that breaks

- `adaptive_grok/util.py:changed_files()` = staged ∪ unstaged ∪ `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, minus `_fingerprint_noise()`.
- `adaptive_grok/util.py:_fingerprint_noise` (shown verbatim in `01-noise-filter.txt`) filters exactly: `.grok-stack/runtime/`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `node_modules`, `vendor`, `*.pyc/*.pyo`, `.coverage`, `coverage/`. There is no entry for the driving agent's own scratch, nor a documented convention that a consumer tree must `.gitignore` it.
- `adaptive_grok/receipts.py:703` then reports `{kind}: stale after repository changes` for a mismatch that has nothing to do with repository changes — the message is misleading at the point of consumption, which is where an agent decides whether to re-run a 30-minute evidence wave.

## Observed consequence in this consumer repo

A review wave bound `code_review`/`test_review` to one fingerprint and `verification` to another, and the tree moved again twice before any of them could be re-recorded. The pipeline can only reach an all-fresh state if the agent stops writing to its own working directory, which it does not control. Two mitigations were attempted locally (committing everything before binding; recording receipts last) — the second one works only while the agent happens not to touch `.qwen/` in between.

## Direction (not a demand)

Either treat agent-owned working directories as noise by name (`.qwen/`, `.claude/`, `.codex/`, …) or, better, make the noise list configuration in `.grok-stack/config/` so a consumer can extend it, and split the staleness reason: `stale after repository changes` vs `stale after agent scratch write`. The second message should tell the agent which path moved, because today the only way to find out is to diff two fingerprints by hand.

## Evidence files

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `00-fingerprint-ab.txt` | A/B run output: fingerprint before/after an unrelated `.qwen/tmp/` file, plus restore |
| `01-noise-filter.txt` | `_fingerprint_noise` verbatim + the `changed_files` command set |

---
